Urumi reference theme — Tempered

Urumi · reference storefront theme · direction v1

Tempereda reference storefront theme for Urumi

One design language for every surface a shopper touches — catalog, cart, checkout, payment, order — built from the store's own materials: its stock, its money, and the states it can be in.

Where it comes from

Three decisions, and what each is answering.

  • tempering colours as state

    An urumi is a ribbon of spring steel. Heat it and it passes through straw, bronze, violet, deep blue — an ordered scale. The store has an ordered scale too: available → held → expiring → released. The palette is that scale, so colour carries stock state instead of decorating it.

  • money is set in mono

    Every price, quantity, SKU, stock count and countdown is set in a wide tabular mono, and nothing else is. The repo's first rule is that money is integer minor units — the type system says the same thing on screen. It also makes columns of figures line up for free.

  • one hairline, never a box

    A single 1px rule is the only divider in the theme — no card borders, no shadows, 2px radius at most. It's what kills the current "three grey boxes" look, and it gives product images the neutral surround photography needs.

Colour

Five neutrals, three signals.

Neutrals are steel-biased rather than pure grey. The three signals are the only saturated colour in the theme, and each one means exactly one thing. Hex values shown are the light theme; every token is redefined for dark.

ink#131A20Text, and every primary button fill.
ground#F1F4F4Page behind the store surface.
surface#FFFFFFWhere products sit.
edge#D2DAD9The hairline. Nothing else.
mute#5A6A70Secondary text, sold-out.
straw#8A6412Brass fitting: focus rings, hover underlines, the wordmark rule.
violet#6B4C9EStock held for you. The one colour shoppers learn.
bronze#96541FHold expiring, or prices unavailable.

Straw is a fitting, not a fill — it never becomes a button background, which keeps every interactive element at full text contrast.

Type

A narrow blade, a plain voice, and a wide ledger.

Three roles, three faces, no overlap. The display face is set narrow because the object the project is named after is a long thin ribbon; the money face is set wide so figures read as objects rather than as text. The contrast between them is the theme's loudest move.

Structure

Four rules that make the rest fall out.

Radius 2px, everywhere

One value. Enough to soften an image corner, not enough to read as a pill.

No shadows, no fills for structure

Depth comes from air and the hairline. A tinted panel only ever means "image goes here".

Asymmetric two-column

Hero and product pages run ~1.2fr / 1fr. Nothing is centred except the page itself.

Motion: one countdown, one hover

The hold timer ticks because it's information. Hover slides a straw rule. That's the whole motion budget.

The page renders the order's own state, never what Stripe's redirect claims — so the state is the first thing on it. Order states

Four more things an order can be.

The confirmation page has six states and is deliberately careful about which it claims. Each gets the same stamp with a different rule, so a shopper who has seen one has read them all. The pending sweep is the hold ribbon again, running indeterminate.

Pending, just back from StripeThe page polls itself for ~30s before offering a manual check. Nothing here claims the order is paid — only the webhook decides that.

Payment submitted.

We're confirming it with our payment provider — this usually takes a few seconds.

Checking3 of 8
FailedThe one fact the buyer needs is that no money moved. It leads.

The payment didn't go through.

No charge was made. Your cart is unchanged — you can try again whenever you're ready.

Back to checkout
ExpiredThe hold lapsed before payment landed. A dead end without the door out, so the door is on the page.

This order expired.

Payment didn't complete in time, so the items went back on sale. Nothing was charged.

Start a new cart
Card payment not set upHonest about whose problem it is. No payable-looking button is ever rendered over an order that can't be paid.

Card payment isn't set up on this store yet. This order can't be placed, nothing has been charged, and your cart is unchanged.

The states nobody designs

Degraded is a look, not a crash.

The theme already renders 200 when the commerce service is unreachable — content survives, money doesn't. That deserves a designed treatment: the continuous hairline breaks into a dashed bronze one. Same device for every partial failure, so it reads the same way every time.

Prices unavailableThe commerce service is unreachable. The catalog still renders.

Prices are unavailable right now. Everything below is up to date — check back in a moment to buy.

Cart pricing degradedQuantities and holds are still exact; only the money is missing.

Totals are unavailable right now. Your quantities and your holds are still exact — you'll see the full total at checkout.

Empty cartAn empty screen is an invitation to act, not an apology.

Nothing held yet.

Your cart is empty. Pick something and we'll hold the stock while you decide.

Applying it

Where the code goes.

The tokens live in one stylesheet the layout imports; every page keeps its scoped <style> block but stops declaring its own colours and spacing. ADR-0003 holds — the plugin keeps serving view models, the theme keeps owning all markup.

  • src/styles/tokens.css

    New. The token block at the top of this page, plus the reset and the three @font-face rules loaded through Astro's font API (self-hosted, no CDN).

  • src/layouts/Base.astro

    Header, wordmark, nav with a live cart count, footer, skip link, and the dark-theme meta. Keeps the inline SVG favicon its test pins — redrawn as the ribbon mark.

  • src/components/

    New: ProductCard, PriceTag, StockRule, HoldRibbon, Notice, MediaPanel, QtyField. Each one renders a view-model field and nothing more.

  • src/pages/index.astro

    Gains the inventory tape. This is the one page that today makes no commerce call — the tape needs one, so it renders the thesis copy alone when the service is down.

  • src/pages/products/*.astro

    Markup swapped for components. No change to the CMS read or the route dispatch.

  • src/pages/cart/index.astro

    The table becomes lines with hold ribbons. expiresAt is already on the wire; the countdown is ~15 lines of client script with a no-JS fallback showing the absolute time.

  • src/pages/checkout/index.astro

    Two panels and the step track. The totals block is the careful part: shipping.label and tax.label can mean "not calculated", and must never render as $0.00 or "Free".

  • src/pages/checkout/pay.astro

    Only the frame changes. Stripe's Payment Element gets an appearance object fed from the same tokens, so its fields match the theme instead of arriving as a default blue widget.

  • src/pages/orders/[orderId].astro

    The state stamp replaces the status paragraph. The bounded meta-refresh poll stays exactly as it is — the sweep is CSS on a page that reloads itself, not new JavaScript.

  • src/lib/error-messages.ts

    No change. The copy in it is already written from the shopper's side, and the mockups quote it verbatim.

Two calls worth arguing with: this reads as Urumi's own brand rather than a neutral starter, on the bet that a fork swaps eight tokens and two faces; and it's light-first, because product photography needs a neutral surround and the dark set is the same tokens inverted.
